title: Add support for nested lists
body:
It would be great if `render()` could handle nested lists. Right now only flat `- item` lists work. Indented items come out as paragraphs. ```python render('- item one\n - nested\n- item two') # Expected: nested
    inside the outer
  • # Actual: indented line becomes a

    ``` Would love to see this supported.

comments.author: riya-dev
comments.body: Good first issue — extend the list handling in the block step. Happy to review.

comments.author: kai-dev
comments.body: Agreed, this comes up a lot. Would make the library a lot more practical.

comments.author: weekend-hacker
comments.body: I started looking at this. The list parser would need a full rewrite to track indentation state properly — pausing for now, it's more involved than I expected.

lesson_feedback: The maintainer called it a good first issue, but a contributor who tried it found the list parser needs a full rewrite. The block step doesn't track indentation state at all — adding nested support isn't an extension, it's a redesign. The difficulty is invisible until you read the code.

reproductionSteps.instruction: Call render('- item one\n  - nested\n- item two').

Observe that the indented line is treated as a

, not a nested

  • .

reproduction.expectedResult: Nested list items render inside an inner <ul>.

buggyBehavior.output:
Indented list item becomes a

tag.

title: Double-underscore bold (__bold__) renders as plain text
body:
The README says both `**bold**` and `__bold__` should produce ``. But `__bold__` just passes through as plain text. ```python render('__bold__') # Returns:

__bold__

# Expected:

bold

``` `**bold**` works fine. Only the double-underscore variant is broken. **Python:** 3.12

comments.author: riya-dev
comments.body: Confirmed. The `__` pattern is missing from `_inline` — only `**` is handled. Thanks for the report.

lesson_feedback: This issue is still open in the tracker but the bug no longer exists. Check the commits tab — the fix landed on 2026-04-22. Reproducing it on HEAD would have caught this immediately: __bold__ now renders correctly.

reproductionSteps.instruction: Open src/mdlite.py and find the _inline function.

Check whether the output is

__bold__

or

bold

.

title: Raw HTML in input passes through into the output unchanged
body:
If you pass a string containing raw HTML to `render()`, it comes out unchanged inside a `

` tag. ```python render('') # Returns:

``` Any application that injects this output into a web page will execute the script. The library should escape `<`, `>`, and `&` before rendering. **Steps to reproduce:** 1. Call `render('')` 2. Observe the output **Expected:** `

<script>alert(1)</script>

` **Actual:** `

` **Python:** 3.12

comments.author: riya-dev
comments.body: Confirmed. The fix goes in `_inline` — call `html.escape(text)` at the very top, before any of the regex patterns run. Please include a test that fails on the current code and passes after your fix.

comments.author: kai-dev
comments.body: Reproduced on Python 3.12 as well. The escape needs to happen before the regexes or the `&` in `<` will get double-processed.

lesson_feedback: Good pick. Clear reproduction steps, confirmed by two maintainers, fix location spelled out in the comments, no PR exists, and the scope is a single line in _inline. This is exactly the kind of issue worth starting with.

reproductionSteps.instruction: Open src/mdlite.py and find the _inline function.

buggyBehavior.output:
Returns "

" — raw HTML passes through unchanged.

fixedBehavior.output:
Returns "

<script>alert(1)</script>

" — HTML characters are safely escaped.

title: Links break sometimes
body:
Sometimes when I use links in my markdown the output doesn't look right. Not sure what's happening.

I'm using Python 3.11.

comments.author: riya-dev
comments.body: Hi, thanks for the report. Could you share the exact markdown string you're passing in and the output you're getting? A short code snippet like `render('[text](url)')` and what it returns would help a lot.

comments.author: confused-first-timer
comments.body: It's all in a large file, I can't really paste it all here. The output just looks wrong in some cases.

lesson_feedback: No input, no output, no specific case. The maintainer asked for a code snippet two days after the report and the response was 'it's in a large file'. You cannot reproduce this, which means you cannot fix it. The right move is to wait for a proper example — or ask for one yourself.

Check whether the actual vs expected output is shown.

title: README example has a typo in the function call
body:
The usage example in README.md has a typo in the function call — it says `form` instead of `from`.

```
form src.mdlite import render
```

Should be:

```
from src.mdlite import render
```

Small fix but confusing for new users.

comments.author: riya-dev
comments.body: Good catch, typo fixes are welcome. Please use a `docs/` branch, e.g. `docs/readme-typo`.

lesson_feedback: A contributor has already claimed this and opened a draft PR (#9) on 2026-09-12. Starting on this without checking first would duplicate their work. Leave a comment asking for an update, or look for another issue.

reproductionSteps.instruction: Open README.md and find the usage example.

reproduction.expectedResult: Import line reads: from src.mdlite import render

buggyBehavior.output: Import line reads: form src.mdlite import render — typo in README.

fixedBehavior.output: Import line reads: from src.mdlite import render
